title: Operator forces regeneration of unchanged content
description:
The content hash is deliberately stable: the same text, voice, and backend
always resolve to the same job. That is correct for caching and wrong for
operations. When a clip generated badly -- a model update, a bad voice, a
truncated render, a backend swapped in place -- the operator has no way to say
"generate this again anyway." `_create_job` short-circuits on
`attribute_not_exists(content_hash)` and returns the existing row.

Forcing regeneration resets the existing record in place rather than minting a
new hash, so the embed on the page keeps resolving to the same clip and picks
up the new audio on its next poll.

## State transition

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pending: POST /jobs
  pending --> claimed: worker claims
  claimed --> done: audio uploaded
  claimed --> failed: generation error
  done --> pending: force regenerate
  failed --> pending: force regenerate
```

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Forcing regeneration of already-generated audio

  Scenario: Operator regenerates a completed clip
    Given a job exists with status "done" and a stored audio object
    When the operator forces regeneration of that content hash
    Then the job status is "pending"
    And the previous audio object is removed from the audio bucket
    And the job has no audio url
    And the cloud fallback is armed for that job

  Scenario: Regeneration keeps the content hash stable
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator forces regeneration of that content hash
    Then the job keeps the same content hash

  Scenario: Regenerating a job that is already pending is rejected
    Given a job exists with status "pending"
    When the operator forces regeneration of that content hash
    Then the response is a conflict
    And the job status is still "pending"

  Scenario: Regeneration issues a fresh job token
    Given a job exists with status "done" and a job token
    When the operator forces regeneration of that content hash
    Then the job token is different from the previous token
```

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`**

- Route: `if method == "POST" and path.endswith("/regenerate") and path.startswith("/admin/jobs/")`
  -> `_regenerate_admin_job(content_hash, headers)`.
- `def _regenerate_admin_job(content_hash: str, headers: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, Any]:`
  - `_require_operator(headers)`
  - Load the item; `LookupError("job_not_found")` when absent.
  - When `item["status"]` is `pending` or `claimed`, raise a conflict
    (add a `ConflictError` mapped to 409 in `handler`'s except chain -- do not
    reuse `ValueError`, the distinction matters to the CLI).
  - Delete the prior S3 object when `audio_key` is set.
  - `job_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`
  - `_jobs.update_item` setting `status = "pending"`, `updated_at`,
    `job_token`, and REMOVE `audio_key`, `claimed_by`, `claim_owner`,
    `claimed_at`, `completed_at`, `failed_at`, `duration_seconds`,
    `error_message`, `worker_type`.
  - Re-arm the fallback: same `_sfn.start_execution` block as `_create_job`,
    with a fresh `baseline_epoch` and the new `job_token`. Extract that block
    from `_create_job` into `_arm_fallback(content_hash, job_token, tts_backend)`
    and call it from both -- one correct path, per AGENTS.md.
  - Return `_response(200, {"content_hash": ..., "status": "pending"})`

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** — `def regenerate_job(self, content_hash: str)`.

**`features/job_management.feature`** — extend with the scenarios above.

## Note on scope

A `force` flag on the public `POST /jobs` (so the embed itself can request
regeneration) is deliberately NOT part of this story. That is a site-key-
authenticated path and would let any embedding page burn GPU at will. If we
want it later it needs its own quota story.

## Acceptance

`make check` green; scenarios pass; `_arm_fallback` is called by both create
and regenerate.

comments.text: Implemented on feature/admin-job-regenerate, merged to develop. POST /admin/jobs/{hash}/regenerate resets a job to pending in place (stable content hash), deletes prior audio, issues a fresh job_token, rearms the Step Functions fallback via a new shared _arm_fallback() helper (also now used by _create_job, replacing duplicated inline logic), rejects pending/claimed jobs with a new ConflictError->409. REMOVE clause independently cross-checked against every attribute _claim_job/_mark_done/_mark_failed can write -- complete. Note for when M11's batch-billing-telemetry lands: that story adds batch_created_at/batch_started_at/batch_stopped_at/container_seconds/provisioning_seconds/billed_seconds/instance_type to job records, none of which are in this REMOVE list yet -- a regenerated job will carry stale billing data from its previous run until that's added. Filed as a coordination follow-up. Confirmed by reverting the handler.py changes that all 4 new scenarios genuinely fail without them. One scenario tightened in review ('keeps the same content hash' asserted against the record's own key, which is vacuously true regardless of whether regeneration ran -- now asserts the API response body instead). Full suite green: black/ruff, pytest (37 passed), behave (23 features, 89 scenarios).
